https://www.politico.eu/article/ursula-v.text: BRUSSELS — European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen sought to smooth over tensions with Spain after Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez accused many of his fellow EU leaders of exploiting the migration crisis in Ceuta to attack his government. In a letter sent to Sánchez on Monday, von der Leyen praised Spain’s handling of the influx of migrants from Morocco into its North African exclave. Her response came after Sánchez wrote to her over the weekend , condemning leaders who “have chosen to attack Spain and to call for its temporary exclusion from the Schengen Area.” Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni on Thursday was the first to propose Spain be suspended from the 29-country Schengen zone in which internal border controls have largely been abolished. Italy and France both imposed restrictions on free movement last week. Advertisement Advertisement Around 50,000 people crossed into Ceuta from Morocco last week, with dozens dying in the attempt. Almost all those who entered have since returned to Morocco. Von der Leyen on Monday praised the “swift handling” of returns by Spanish and Moroccan authorities, saying they had “successfully prevent[ed] illegal movement onwards to mainland Spain and Europe.” The exchange followed a joint letter from 22 EU leaders at the weekend calling for an emergency meeting of interior ministers and a tougher, coordinated response to the crisis. That meeting will take place on Tuesday, with EU ambassadors discussing the situation on Monday afternoon. The intervention by EU leaders opened a new political fight over Spain’s migration policy, including Madrid’s plan to regularize more than 1 million undocumented migrants. Some governments argued that the measure created a “pull factor” by encouraging people to believe that irregular entry could eventually lead to legal residency. Sánchez rejected that criticism in his letter, accusing some EU countries of responding in a “selfish,” “polarizing” and unlawful manner. He argued that Spain needed European solidarity rather than blame after the deaths and the strain placed on Ceuta’s authorities. The Spanish government refused to comment for this article. Von der Leyen’s letter offered that solidarity while making clear that the crisis would also have to prompt stronger EU action. Advertisement Advertisement “Migration is a European challenge that requires a European response,” she wrote. “And in this, solidarity is fundamental.” The Commission, she said, had offered Spain financial and operational support, with Frontex, Europol and the EU asylum agency ready to assist. Migration Commissioner Magnus Brunner on Friday told Spanish Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska that the bloc was willing to “increase support for Spain” to “control the situation,” and to deploy members of Frontex, the EU agency that supports member countries in monitoring and managing the EU’s external borders, to Ceuta. Frontex currently has staff deployed in Ceuta, as well as on the Canary Islands and parts of the Andalusian coastline. An official watches as people gather at the border between Morocco and Spain on July 31, 2026. | Abdel Majid Bziouat/AFP via Getty Images Madrid has repeatedly declined to request that the agency’s presence in Spain be increased, insisting that border control falls under the jurisdiction of national authorities. Following a surge in migrant arrivals to Ceuta in 2021, and an increase in arrivals to the Canary Islands in 2024, Spain’s interior ministry rejected calls to ask for Frontex’s support, insisting it had sufficient resources to manage the situation. ‘We must do more’ Von der Leyen said the incident had exposed weaknesses in the bloc’s border management. “It is clear that we must do more to further strengthen our borders at critical points,” the Commission president wrote, including through “vigilant monitoring and the use of physical barriers where needed.” She outlined five priorities: preventing irregular migration through stronger cooperation with partner countries, reinforcing the EU’s external borders, establishing early-warning systems, dismantling smuggling networks, and improving returns. Advertisement Advertisement Morocco, she said, remained an “important strategic partner” in combating migrant smuggling and irregular migration. The EU should work with Rabat and Madrid to improve early-warning systems around Ceuta and Melilla, as well as technical and financial support for Morocco, she said. Von der Leyen also endorsed the emergency meeting of the EU’s justice and home affairs ministers on Tuesday, describing it as a first step toward a collective response. The ministers should agree on a way forward before EU leaders assess the measures at their next European Council meeting, she said. “Spain and its people can count on the enduring support of the Commission,” von der Leyen concluded.

https://telex.hu/techtud/2026/08/28/mohu.text: Menü Kereső Kötelezővé kellene tenni a biohulladék szelektív gyűjtését, hogy teljesíteni tudjuk az uniós vállalásokat Techtud Belföld Legfontosabb Biohulladék-gyűjtők ürítése Budapest XX. kerületében 2024 novemberében – Fotó: Bődey János / Telex Thüringer Barbara Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Annak ellenére, hogy a korábbi tervek szerint 1,5-2 millió embernek szerették volna lehetővé tenni a biohulladék szelektív gyűjtését, az elmúlt másfél évben gyakorlatilag alig történt valami ezen a területen – derült ki a Mohu háttérbeszélgetésén. Ennek a tapasztalataik szerint az az oka, hogy a pilotprogramban részt vevő 14 településen sem sikerült számottevő eredményeket elérni a lakosság, illetve a közös képviselők ellenállása miatt. Ezért a cég szerint az infrastruktúra fejlesztése és a szemléletformáló kampányok önmagukban nem elegendőek, csak az vezethetne eredményre, ha ezzel egy időben kötelezővé tennék a biohulladék szelektív gyűjtését – ezt azonban hiába jelezték az előző kormányzatnak, az a választás előtt nem akarta ezt felvállalni. De hogy jutottunk idáig? 2018-ban született meg az a döntés az Európai Unióban (a hulladék-keretirányelv), ami a tagországokat, így Magyarországot is arra kötelezi, hogy 2023. december 31-től elkezdjék a háztartási biohulladék szelektív gyűjtését. Az unió azt a célt tűzte ki, hogy 2035-re a hulladék 65 százalékát újra kell hasznosítani – miközben az Eurostat 2024-es legfrissebb adatai szerint az unió országaiban átlagosan ez 48 százalék volt, addig Magyarországon mindössze 34 százalék. Kutatások szerint Magyarországon a háztartási hulladék 30 százaléka konyhai hulladék, ami főként a hulladéklerakókban (évente 400 ezer tonna) vagy a csatornarendszerben (évente 600 ezer tonna) végzi. Ez azért hatalmas probléma, mert a kidobott élelmiszerek nagy mértékben növelik a metánkibocsátást, és ezáltal jelentősen hozzájárulnak az éghajlatváltozáshoz. A koncessziót elnyerő Mohu Mol Hulladékgazdálkodási Zrt. 2024-ben országszerte 14 település társasházi övezeteiben indította el a biohulladék szelektív gyűjtését pilotprogramként: Budapesten a XI., a XX. és a XXI. kerület egyes társasházi övezeteiben, Miskolcon, Debrecenben, Székesfehérváron, Szolnokon, Kecskeméten, Cegléden, Zalaegerszegen, Békéscsabán, Nagykanizsán, Tatabányán, Kaposváron, Gyulán, valamint Békés városának egyes körzeteiben. 2024 októberéig a pilotprogram 460 ezer emberhez jutott el, akiknek a harmada, nagyjából 140 ezer ember igényelt biohulladék tárolására alkalmas kukákat. Míg Miskolcon, Szolnokon, Székesfehérváron és Tatabányán a pilotban elért lakosság 100 százaléka csatlakozott a programhoz, máshol, így például Budapesten nehézségekbe ütközött a szelektív gyűjtés bevezetése. A Mohu háztartási 5 literes gyűjtőedényeiben a programban részt vevő háztartások külön gyűjthetnék többek között a gyümölcsök és a zöldségek maradékait, a kávézaccot, a tojáshéjat, a főtt ételmaradékokat (a húsokat is, de a csontokról leválasztva), a pékárukat és a tejtermékeket is – egy fontos szempont van csak, mindezt műanyag csomagolás nélkül kellene beletenni. A begyűjtött biohulladékot a háztartások a társasházaknak biztosított, 120 literes barna kukákba dobhatják ki, amiket hetente egy-két alkalommal ürítenek a Mohu szerződött partnerei, akik biogázüzemekbe szállítják azt, ahol villamos energiát lehet belőle előállítani, vagy komposzttelepre viszik, amiből a mezőgazdaság részesül. Ez idáig mind szépen hangzik, azonban az embereket nem lehetett arról meggyőzni, hogy semmivel sem büdösebb, ha szelektíven gyűjtik az ételmaradékaikat, mint ha kidobják a sima szemetesbe – pedig a háztartási gyűjtők szag- és kifolyásmentesen záródnak. Az sem segített, hogy a kezdeti begyűjtési nehézségek miatt előfordult, hogy néhány gyűjtőkukában kukacok ütötték fel a fejüket. Ez vezetett ahhoz, hogy míg korábban úgy számolt a Mohu, hogy hetente 50–90 deka biohulladékot fognak kidobni az emberek, ez az első próbaév végére csak a 30 dekát érte el. Ez volt az oka annak, hogy 2024 végén úgy döntött a cég, hogy a korábban kitűzött 1,5-2 milliós bővítést lejjebb veszik, és kisebb lépésekben haladnak tovább a rendszer bővítésével. Végül azonban még ez a kisebb léptékű bővítés is elmaradt, mert a cég inkább arra próbált meg először koncentrálni, hogy a már a programban részt vevő településeken vigye feljebb az eredményeket. Mint a háttérbeszélgetésen Runtág Tivadar, a Mohu stratégiai és fenntarthatósági igazgatója elmondta, annyit sikerült elérniük, hogy a 140 ezer emberről feltornászták 230 ezerre a programban részt vevők számát. Elvileg ennyien vesznek most részt a gyűjtésben. Gyakorlatilag viszont csak annyit tudnak, hogy ennyi embert érnek el a társasházaknak kiosztott 120 literes barna kukákkal és az otthoni 5 literes edényekkel – de, hogy ebből valójában hányan használják is azokat, arra nincsenek konkrét számok. A begyűjtött mennyiségek azonban arról árulkodnak, hogy nagyon kevesen. Biohulladék a gyűjtőkben Budapest XX. kerületében 2024 novemberében – Fotó: Bődey János / Telex Az Orbán-kormány nem vállalta fel a népszerűtlen intézkedést „A kukák töltöttsége minimális” – jellemezte a helyzetet Pártl-Konrád Brigitta, a Mohu termékmenedzsere, aki elmondta, hogy jelenleg a 10 százalékát érik el annak a mennyiségnek, amivel korábban számolt a cég. Mint mondta, a vegyes hulladékban jelenleg található konyhai zöld- és élelmiszer-hulladék alapján a maximálisan begyűjthető mennyiség 53 kilogramm/fő/év lenne, ehhez képest most ott tartanak, hogy évente átlagban 5-6 kiló jött össze fejenként. Ha a teljes lakosságra ki tudnák terjeszteni a szelektív gyűjtést, akkor évi nagyjából 500 ezer tonnát tudnának begyűjteni. A most a program által elért 460 ezer lakosnál ez évente 24 380 tonnát jelentene. Mivel nagyjából feleennyien csatlakoztak csak, a maximális begyűjthető mennyiség 12 ezer tonna lenne évente – a valóság azonban kiábrándító, ugyanis mindössze 1200 tonna begyűjtött mennyiségről tudnak beszámolni. És még ez az arány is romlott 2025-ről 2026-ra: a vizsgált féléveket tekintve 2026-ban vidéken a 2025-ös mennyiség 90 százalékát, míg Budapesten a 68 százalékát sikerült begyűjteni. Míg Budapesten az eleve nagyon kis mennyiség is jócskán visszaesett, vidéken néhány településen egy kicsivel nőtt: Miskolcon, Zalaegerszegen, Gyulán és Nagykanizsán. Ezek a számok olyan szinten maradtak el a várakozásoktól, hogy a Mohunak nem volt más választása, mint rálépni a fékre, és a tervezett bővítés helyett megpróbálni a szabályozói oldalról eredményeket elérni. Információink szerint az előző kormányzatnál azt szerette volna elérni a cég, hogy legalább a kukákat kötelező legyen átvenniük a társasházak közös képviselőinek, de valójában amellett kardoskodtak, hogy az lenne a legcélravezetőbb, ha az uniós cél eléréséhez kötelezővé tennék a háztartásoknak a szelektív gyűjtést. Az Orbán-kormány azonban a választások előtt nem vállalt fel egy ilyen feltehetően népszerűtlen szigorítást. Az EU-ban vannak példák ilyen szigorításra. Szlovéniában például ha a biohulladékot a kommunális kukába dobják, akkor akár 4-500 eurós büntetést is ki lehetne szabni az adott társasházra – erre azonban sok esetben nem kerül sor, mert a figyelmeztetés bőven elegendő ahhoz, hogy az esetleges szankció súlyossága miatt betartsák az emberek a szabályokat. Szakértők szerint itthon is elengedhetetlen lenne a szabályozás szigorítása, valamint az, hogy az állam és az önkormányzatok is szerepet vállaljanak a lakossági tájékoztatásban és szemléletformálásban. Úgy tudjuk, hogy a Mohu és az új kormányzat között most abban már egyetértés mutatkozik, hogy a biohulladék begyűjtésének komoly szerepe van az uniós kötelezettségek teljesítésében. A jelenlegi hulladékgyűjtési rendszer jövője azonban nemcsak a biohulladék terén, hanem általában is kérdéses: Gajdos László élő környezetért felelős miniszter néhány napja bejelentette, hogy tárgyalásokat kezdenek a Mohuval, és felülvizsgálják a 35 évre szóló hulladékgazdálkodási koncessziót. „Kemény partnerek leszünk. A nemzeti érdek és a lakosság magas színvonalú kiszolgálása érdekében mindent el fogunk követni” – írta a miniszter . Azzal, hogy miért fontos a biohulladék szelektív gyűjtése, több cikkben is foglalkoztunk: Komposztország leszünk, ha akarjuk, ha nem Lehet, hogy picit büdös lesz az új kuka, de azért menő Itt kapják meg először a biokukájukat az emberek Kukaokosító: minden, amit a biohulladék szelektív gyűjtéséről tudni kell Három városban már elindult, Budapesten csak márciusban kezdődik a biohulladék szelektív gyűjtése Ha engem fejbe csapnának, se tudnék ilyen hülyeséget kitalálni – gyanakvással fogadják az emberek a biokukákat Kong a kuka: nehezen indul be a biohulladék szelektív gyűjtése „Üzenem a Mohunak, hogy ez egy elmebaj” Szomorú, de a magyar az ilyen sajnos Kedvenceink Partnereinktől Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/12/germ.text: German energy and infrastructure heavyweights are exploring new opportunities in Azerbaijan. Their plans cover both gas supplies and renewable energy, at a time when Europe seeks to reduce its dependence on Russian fossil fuels.Speaking at the German-Azerbaijani Connectivity Conference 2026, which was hosted by the German-Azerbaijani Chamber of Commerce (AHK Azerbaijan) in Baku, European corporate leaders outlined concrete investment plans ranging from fossil fuels to renewable energy networks along the Middle Corridor.The gathering brought together more than 250 participants, including over 35 guests from Germany and Azerbaijani policymakers.A new pillar of economic cooperationNargis Wieck, Executive Director of AHK Azerbaijan, stressed the need to build on strong bilateral trade ties to encourage concrete investments.Wieck told Euronews that one of the key questions was how to “deepen our economic cooperation through concrete projects”. She also said that part of the chamber’s role involves “helping German companies become part of Azerbaijan’s economic ecosystem, and Azerbaijani companies integrate more closely into German and European value chains”. German Ambassador Dirk Lölke noted that after President Ilham Aliyev’s recent visit to Berlin, regional connectivity could become the "second pillar" of bilateral economic relations, alongside energy cooperation.Accelerating the green energy transitionOn the energy front, Siemens Energy said it was ready to provide critical technology and expertise for Azerbaijan’s renewable energy sector and the planned Caspian-Black Sea-Europe Green Energy Corridor.Frederik Doye, Senior Vice President for Europe at Siemens Energy, emphasised that Azerbaijan’s vast offshore wind potential positions the country as a vital energy link connecting Europe, the South Caucasus, and Central Asia.Azerbaijan plans to develop 8 GW of wind and solar projects by 2032, according to Deputy Minister of Energy Elnur Soltanov.He said that the priority was to develop the partnership in a number of areas, including "renewable energy, energy connectivity, energy efficiency and the broader energy transition"."Our goal is to connect this potential to European markets through several complementary routes - the Caspian-Black Sea-Europe Green Energy Corridor, the Central Asia-Azerbaijan Corridor, and westward links to Türkiye and Europe via Georgia and Nakhchivan," he added.Beyond generation, German technology providers are setting their sights on power grid modernisation, battery energy storage systems (BESS), and electric vehicle charging infrastructure.Julia Egel, Head of Stakeholder Engagement at AHK Azerbaijan, noted that German firms are perfectly positioned to support Azerbaijan's mandate to boost renewable power generation. The country's stated target is to increase the share of renewables in its installed electricity generation capacity to 30% by 2030.Egel also announced an upcoming trade mission of German energy companies to Azerbaijan, with plans for targeted business-to-business meetings and potential German pavilions at next year's Baku Energy Week.Securing gas suppliesAlongside renewable energy projects, German companies are looking to secure gas supplies. German gas importer VNG AG said it was interested in a long-term supply agreement with the State Oil Company of Azerbaijan (SOCAR) lasting 15 to 20 years.The firm aims to significantly boost current import volumes to stabilise European markets in the short term before transitioning to fully decarbonised systems. The company also said it was interested in working more closely with SOCAR on biomethane, renewable energy, hydrogen and decarbonised fuels.Separately, German wind turbine manufacturer Enercon is exploring the possibility of setting up local production in Azerbaijan using German financing and technology."We are currently exploring investment opportunities in Azerbaijan and how we, as a wind turbine manufacturer, can become active here," company representative Tayfun Bayraktar said on the sidelines of the conference.While the company has not yet received a formal proposal, Bayraktar noted that successful talks could eventually lead to a local manufacturing facility with export potential.He added that the size of any investment would depend on demand, with a single 7 MW wind turbine currently costing around €7 million to €8 million.Digitalising the Middle CorridorBeyond energy, the conference also focused on logistics and digital infrastructure.As Azerbaijan pushes to expand its role along the Middle Corridor, the German business community is stepping up its logistical support. Azerbaijan expects total transit cargo passing through the country to reach 30 million tonnes by 2030.Deputy Minister of Economy Samad Bashirli presented the Alat Free Economic Zone as a platform for German manufacturers to establish export-oriented production, citing the country's stable macroeconomic environment.Deputy Minister of Digital Development and Transport Rashad Hasanov emphasised Azerbaijan's ambition to become a regional base for global tech firms.He underlined the importance of digitalisation in improving the Middle Corridor's efficiency and strengthening Azerbaijan’s role as a bridge between Europe and Asia.

https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/14/one-.text: At least one person was killed and more than 20 others injured in a Russian attack on Ukraine’s capital Kyiv overnight into Wednesday.A large fire broke out in a residential building after it had come under Russian shelling.The strikes targeted a key power plant in the city, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.Zelenskyy noted that the Darnytska CHP-4 plant, which supplies the capital with heating and electricity, was targeted by a ballistic missile.The attack comes just days after US President Donald Trump announced an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, halting attacks on energy targets.Since then, the Kremlin’s nightly attacks have nevertheless continued to target energy sites, according to Zelenskyy.What 'energy ceasefire'?The attacks also come at a dire time for Ukraine, currently grappling with a crisis which has seen more than 600,000 people lose power in various strikes on energy grids."Energy facilities in Kyiv and the surrounding region have come under a massive ballistic missile strike. There are power disruptions in the capital," Mayor Vitali Klitschko wrote on Telegram.The Ukrainian President accused Moscow of disrespecting US President Donald Trump and his "energy ceasefire"."The strike was entirely deliberate and demonstrative in its scale –- Russia has never before shown such ostentatious disrespect toward the United States", Zelenskyy wrote on X.Meanwhile Russia said it had shot down 900 Ukrainian drones overnight, including 180 near Moscow.Zelenskyy has previously noted that Ukraine is prepared to abide by Trump’s truce if Russia reciprocates, a plea the Kremlin did not acknowledge.

https://www.dw.com/en/bombed-factories-b.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5PnVh Prefer DW on Google Foreign companies operating in Ukraine see big opportunities, but also face substantial risks Image: Sergey Bobok/AFP Advertisement Power plants, train stations, shopping centers, warehouses and residential buildings: The massive Russian attacks on civilian targets across Ukraine continue unabated. Industrial facilities have also come under fire, affecting German companies. "Over the past few months, goods and facilities worth several hundred million euros have gone up in smoke," reported Oliver Gierlichs, who heads Bayer's operations in Ukraine and serves as president of the German-Ukrainian Chamber of Industry and Commerce (AHK Ukraine). The damage is estimated at €500 million ($544 million). At the 9th German-Ukrainian Business Forum, held in Berlin on November 20, Gierlichs described the situation on the ground. Together with two other German business associations, the AHK had invited around 500 participants from politics and industry, including German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi. According to the AHK, just over 2,000 German companies are active in Ukraine. German direct investment in the country totals around €1 billion ($1.1 billion). The situation remains critical due to the ongoing attacks, Gierlichs said. "We are preparing for a difficult winter." Made in Germany — Rebuilding Ukraine To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Ukrainian economy under pressure After posting comparatively strong growth rates in recent years, Ukraine's economy has slowed sharply since the summer. "The intensified Russian attacks on Ukraine's critical infrastructure and production capacity in recent months have significantly worsened the economic outlook," according to the latest analysis by the Kyiv School of Economics (KSE), which warns of "substantial risks." Energy supplies are under strain, and electricity remains in short supply. Companies are also grappling with a worker shortage, as many people have been mobilized for military service or have fled abroad to escape the attacks. German business leaders also cite burdensome approval processes and unclear regulations in Ukraine. "Not a single German company has left Ukraine since the start of this war," Merz emphasized at the business forum. He also pointed out that "in 2025, trade between Germany and Ukraine exceeded €12 billion, an increase of 4.4% compared with the previous year." Germany continues to supply large quantities of defense equipment, but new capabilities are increasingly being developed through joint ventures. At the business forum, held at the House of German Business Associations in Berlin, the long-range combat drone "Anubis," produced by the German-Ukrainian joint venture Auterion Airlogix, was displayed in the foyer. The drone was developed in Ukraine and the software in Germany. A total of 5,000 drones are to be produced near Munich. This marks the first time Germany has established industrial-scale production of heavy attack drones on its own soil. "Through this cooperation, Germany's technological capacity for innovation is expanding in ways that would have been unimaginable just a few years ago," Merz said. The chancellor is convinced that cooperation between the two countries will also benefit Germany's civilian industries. "What we invest in Ukraine today will be repaid many times over through stability, export opportunities, joint projects, and economic growth," he said. Half a trillion dollars needed for reconstruction For foreign companies operating in Ukraine, it is a continuous balancing act. On the one hand, substantial risks persist; on the other, Ukraine represents a land of opportunity, with a market size virtually unmatched anywhere else in Europe. In February 2025, the European Commission and the Ukrainian government estimated that Ukraine would need $524 billion in funding for reconstruction and recovery over the following 10 years. This figure has likely grown even larger since then. In this context, Ukraine is increasingly seen not merely as a recipient of aid but also as a potential future business destination. The country aims to modernize its economy, bring it into alignment with EU standards, and achieve deeper integration into the European single market over the long term. Can Ukraine still count on Germany? "German expertise and Ukrainian drive, combined with unity and determination, make for a powerful partnership," Oliver Gierlichs noted. However, achieving this will require greater support, the AHK president emphasized. "Companies need reliable financing and investment guarantees, as well as effective instruments to protect themselves against war-related risks." Reliable logistics, predictable business conditions, and faster administrative procedures will also be essential, he added. Investment guarantees and reforms as prerequisites for new projects At the business forum, Chancellor Merz pledged support in these areas while also calling on Ukraine to pursue further reforms, particularly to strengthen the rule of law and combat corruption. "These reforms are a prerequisite for additional financial assistance and investment." Another challenge stems from the differing interests of the partners. German companies are seeking to expand into new markets, while their Ukrainian counterparts seek technology transfers and local production to keep as much value creation as possible in the country. "Export fees or legal restrictions on the transfer of intellectual property rights stand in the way of joint innovation efforts," the chancellor cautioned. Representatives of Ukrainian business associations estimate that the private sector could cover up to 40% of Ukraine's reconstruction costs in the long term. For now, however, many projects rely on support from international development banks, government guarantees, or public funding programs. Without such support, many investments would be difficult to undertake. In principle, business investment follows a straightforward model: Companies commit their own capital and bear the losses if a venture fails commercially. When bank loans are involved, the risk is initially shared by the company and the lending institution. Government-backed projects are different. When investment guarantees are in place, companies are compensated for any losses incurred. This does not apply when companies incur losses as a result of their own business decisions. Compensation may, however, be available in cases involving political actions, such as expropriation, or when war destroys assets and disrupts operations. Under a government guarantee, the taxpayer ultimately bears the risk in such circumstances. By the end of 2025, the German government had provided investment guarantees covering a total investment volume of €558 million ($611 million) in Ukraine. German companies hoping to benefit from Ukraine's reconstruction need to establish partnerships and build a long-term presence in the country now. After all, the competition is already heating up. At the German-Ukrainian Business Forum, participants noted that German business leaders have often been more risk-averse than their counterparts from Turkey, India and China. International interest in Ukraine's reconstruction is considerable, and German companies are far from the only ones vying for contracts. This article was originally written in German.
